belief: People are just waiting for me to die.
origins: When family talks about wills, care homes, or logistics, an older adult can hear impatience. Isolation, and the absence of visitors, can seem to confirm it. Some begin to feel like a burden or an inconvenience.
teaches: God says, “Even to your old age, I will be the same, and I will bear you up when you turn gray. I have made you, and I will carry you; I will sustain you and deliver you” (Isaiah 46:4). “Do not discard me in my old age; do not forsake me when my strength fails” is a prayer God answers. “You are to rise in the presence of the elderly, honor the aged, and fear your God” (Leviticus 19:32). Honoring the aged is God’s command, and many love you. If you ever feel that life is not worth living, call or text 988 or tell someone now.
self_statements: My family is counting the days.
errors: Believing I am either wanted or waiting to die.
Feeling lonely and concluding that I am unwanted.
questions: What have people actually said or done that makes me feel this way?
Who has shown that they love me?
Have I told someone how I feel?
What does God say about my years?
What could I ask my family for?
Who could I connect with, like a church friend or neighbor?
truth: God will carry me to old age and beyond, and He commands respect for the elderly. I matter to Him and to people who love me. I can say what I feel, ask for time together, and reach out for support.
hw_truths: The elderly are to be honored.
log: Each week, note one visit, call, or kind word you received or gave.
actions: Share how you feel with a family member or friend.
Connect with a senior group or church class.
If you feel life is not worth living, call or text 988 (U.S.).
prayer: Lord, I fear being waited out. You have promised to carry me. Surround me with people who love me, and let me know that I matter. Amen.
